text.short: Boise, Grove Street. A boarding house that took Basque men from 1917 to 1969, and has been the country's first Basque museum since 1985.
text.history: Cyrus Jacobs built the brick house in 1864. Basque families ran it as a boarding house; the Uberuagas took it on in 1917, bought it in 1928, and kept boarders until 1969. Adelia Simplot, a Basque immigrant's daughter, bought it from the family and opened the museum inside it in 1985.

sections.heading: Why it matters to a directory of restaurants
sections.body: Every long table in this directory descends from a room like this one — a bed, a meal at a set hour, somebody who spoke Euskara, and a table long enough for everyone in the building. California and Nevada kept the table and lost the building. Boise kept the building.

founded.note: as a house; a Basque boarding house from the 1910s; a museum since 1985
